'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Cultural Heritage of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Cultural Properties == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== Location & Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun part_of''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun part_of - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun part_of''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun part_of (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun part_of).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Cultural Properties == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun part_of''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== Location & Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun part_of''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Cultural Properties == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== Location & Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-typed tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-typed tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-typed''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-typed tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-typed, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Cultural Properties == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== Location & Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.

In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>

Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image募集中|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | latitude = 33.3262 | longitude = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | artifacts = | designated = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== Location & Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== Location & Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== Location & Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>

The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>

Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>

But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image募集中|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | latitude = 33.3262 | longitude = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | artifacts = | designated = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
== References == {{Reflist}}
== External Links == * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656 '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site''' (Agency for Cultural Affairs, Japan)]

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
