'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designated as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>

The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designated as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designated a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designation1 as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designation1 as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been designation1 as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the former Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>

Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image募集中|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | other_designation1 = National other_other_designation of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been other_designation1 as a '''National other_other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Plattype-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_other_designation == '''National other_other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been other_designation1 as a '''National other_other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Plattype-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_other_designation == '''National other_other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been other_designation1 as a '''National other_other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Plattype-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_other_designation == '''National other_other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_other_designation"/>

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been other_designation1 as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>

The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Plattype-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>

The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been other_designation1 as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Plattype-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)

Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image募集中|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | other_designation1 = National other_designation of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been other_designation1 as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Plattype-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
== References == {{Reflist}}
== External Links == * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656 '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation''' (Agency for Cultural Affairs, Japan)]

In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m

Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image募集中|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | other_designation1 = National other_designation of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been other_designation1 as a '''National other_designation''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National other_designation">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|other_designation of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Plattype-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was other_designation1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was other_designation1 a '''National other_designation'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National other_designation other_designation''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National other_designation"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== other_designation == '''National other_designation''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National other_designation"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
