'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|12=draft}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.

The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>

So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image募集中|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|12=draft}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|12=draft}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|12=draft}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
== References == {{Reflist}}
== External Links == * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656 '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site''' (Agency for Cultural Affairs, Japan)]
* {{ill|Ōtsuka Kofun|en}}

So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image募集中|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|12=draft}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|12=draft}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|12=draft}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
== References == {{Reflist}}
== External Links == * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656 '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site''' (Agency for Cultural Affairs, Japan)]

{{日本の古墳 |名称 = 田主丸大塚古墳 |画像 = {{画像募集中|cat=久留米市}} |別名 = |所属 = 田主丸古墳群 |所在地 = [[福岡県]][[久留米市]]田主丸町石垣
（大塚古墳歴史公園内） |緯度度 = 33|緯度分 = 19|緯度秒 = 34.17 |経度度 =130|経度分 = 42|経度秒 = 41.55 |ISO = JP-40 |形状 = [[前方後円墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長103m |築造時期 = [[6世紀]]後半 |埋葬施設 = [[横穴式石室]] |被葬者 = |出土品 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「田主丸大塚古墳」
（「田主丸古墳群」に包含） |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Fukuoka |ラベル = 田主丸
大塚古墳 |アイコン = 前方後円墳-南南西 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''田主丸大塚古墳'''（たぬしまるおおつかこふん）は、[[福岡県]][[久留米市]][[田主丸町]]石垣にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。田主丸古墳群を構成する古墳の1つ。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「田主丸古墳群」のうち）。 == 概要 == 福岡県南部、[[耳納山地]]北麓の[[筑後平野]]を一望する台地（標高70-80メートル）上に築造された大型前方後円墳である{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}{{Sfn|田主丸古墳群（国指定史跡）}}。一帯では本古墳のほか[[装飾古墳]]の寺徳古墳・中原狐塚古墳・西館古墳などが分布し、本古墳はそれら田主丸古墳群の中で最大規模になる{{Sfn|田主丸古墳群（平凡社）|2004}}。墳丘は現在までに前方部の大半が開墾等により削平されている。古くは[[江戸時代]]の『筑後将士軍談』に記述が見えるほか{{Sfn|郷土の文化財|2008|pp=1-4}}、これまでに数次の発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は前方後円形（発掘調査以前は円形と認識）で、前方部を南方向の斜面上方部に向ける{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}。墳丘外表では[[埴輪]]は認められていないが、[[葺石]]が認められており{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}、石垣状に構築されるという特徴を示す。また墳丘後円部には[[造出]]を付す{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}。埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]であるが、内部は未調査のため詳細は明らかでない{{Sfn|田主丸古墳群（国指定史跡）}}。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]後半頃（または6世紀後半-末頃{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}）と推定される。当時は[[磐井の乱]]（6世紀前半）後の統制で前方後円墳の築造が停止に至る時期であり、全国的にも大型古墳の数は少ないが、それでありながら当地に大型前方後円墳として築造された点で築造背景が注目される古墳になる{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳II|2014|pp=17-21}}。また久留米では大規模遺跡として[[高良山神籠石]]（高良山城）が知られており、その築城を巡る背景として、本古墳の石垣状葺石に古代山城の石積技術の下地を見る説や{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳II|2014|pp=17-21}}、[[7世紀]]前半頃まで使用形跡がある本古墳と高良山神籠石との関連を推測する説がある[https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html 『第4回神籠石サミット 久留米（史跡高良山神籠石）大会 パンフレット』] 第4回神籠石サミット久留米大会実行委員会、2009年、p. 16（リンクは久留米市ホームページ）。。 古墳域は[[1993年]]（[[平成]]5年）に旧田主丸町指定史跡に指定され、[[2002年]]（平成14年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定された。現在は史跡整備のうえで大塚古墳歴史公園として公開されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[江戸時代]]後期、[[久留米藩]]の学者の矢野一貞の『筑後将士軍談』に「当国第一ノ大塚」と記述{{Sfn|郷土の文化財|2008|pp=1-4}}。 * [[1977年]]（昭和52年）の『福岡県遺跡等分布地図』に円墳の「大塚3号墳」として記載{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳|2001|pp=1-3}}。 * [[1992年]]（[[平成]]4年度）、確認調査（旧田主丸町教育委員会）{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳|2001|pp=1-3}}{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳II|2014|pp=1-2}}。 * [[1993年]]（平成5年）7月7日、旧田主丸町指定史跡に指定史跡説明板。。 * [[1995年|1995]]・[[1997年|1997]]-[[2001年]]度（平成7・9-13年度）、第1-5次発掘調査。大型前方後円墳と判明（旧田主丸町教育委員会）{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳|2001|pp=1-3}}{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳II|2014|pp=1-2}}。 * [[2002年]]（平成14年）3月19日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「田主丸古墳群」のうち）。 * [[2005年]]度（平成17年度）、古墳北側の史跡整備（久留米市教育委員会）。 * [[2006年|2006]]・[[2013年]]度（平成18・25年度）、第6・7次発掘調査（久留米市教育委員会）{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳II|2014|pp=1-2}}。 * 2013-[[2014年]]度（平成25-26年度）、第2期史跡整備（久留米市教育委員会）[https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html 大塚古墳歴史公園の史跡部分の整備が完了しました]（久留米市ホームページ）。。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}。 * 墳丘長：103メートル * 後円部 直径：60メートル * 前方部 幅：45メートル 前方部は大きく削平を受けているため、墳丘上面の様相は明らかでなく、史跡整備では模式的な墳丘の表現にとどめられている。 付帯施設としては、後円部西側に台形状に張り出す[[造出]]が存在する。この造出は、後円部側幅11.5メートル、先端部幅7.5メートル、長さ12.3メートルを測る。ただし墳丘上面は削平されているため、詳細は明らかでない。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設は、後円部西側くびれ部付近における[[横穴式石室]]。発掘調査では石室入り口の前庭部が認められており、通路幅は2.45メートル、右側壁高さは4メートルを測る。この石室の詳細は未調査であるが、周辺古墳の様相から壁画の存在可能性が推測される。この墓道からは[[7世紀]]前半頃の土器が出土している{{Sfn|田主丸古墳群（平凡社）|2004}}。 == 文化財 == === 国の史跡 === * 田主丸大塚古墳（史跡「田主丸古墳群」のうち） *: 2002年（平成14年）3月19日、既指定の史跡「寺徳古墳」に田主丸大塚古墳ほか古墳2基を追加指定、名称を「田主丸古墳群」に変更{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|2656|田主丸古墳群}}。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[福岡県]][[久留米市]]田主丸町石垣（大塚古墳歴史公園内） '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道：[[九州旅客鉄道]]（JR九州）[[久大本線]] [[田主丸駅]]（徒歩約40分） '''周辺''' * 田主丸古墳群 ** 寺徳古墳 ** 中原狐塚古墳 ** 西館古墳 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 史跡説明板（久留米市2015年設置板ほか） * 地方自治体発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2001|chapter=|title=田主丸大塚古墳 -福岡県浮羽郡田主丸町所在の古墳の史跡範囲確認調査報告-|series=田主丸町文化財調査報告書第15集|publisher=田主丸町教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|田主丸大塚古墳|2001}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|author=|chapter={{PDFlink|[https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3010bunkazai/files/P13-28.pdf 田主丸古墳群]}}|year=2008|title=郷土の文化財|publisher=久留米市教育委員会|isbn=|page=1-4|ref={{Harvid|郷土の文化財|2008}}}} - リンクは久留米市ホームページ。 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2014|chapter=|title=田主丸大塚古墳II -第6・7次調査-|series=久留米市文化財調査報告書第348集|publisher=久留米市教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|田主丸大塚古墳II|2014}}}} * 事典類 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=赤司善彦|year=2002|chapter=大塚古墳 > 田主丸大塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|田主丸大塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=|chapter=[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%94%B0%E4%B8%BB%E4%B8%B8%E5%8F%A4%E5%A2%B3%E7%BE%A4-1444396 田主丸古墳群]|title=国指定史跡ガイド|publisher=[[講談社]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|田主丸古墳群（国指定史跡）}}}} - リンクは朝日新聞社「コトバンク」。 == 外部リンク == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|2656|田主丸古墳群}} {{デフォルトソート:たぬしまるおおつかこふん}} [[Category:福岡県の古墳]] 田主丸大塚古墳（史跡「田主丸古墳群」のうち） *: 2002年（平成14年）3月19日、既指定の史跡「寺徳古墳」に田主丸大塚古墳ほか古墳2基を追加指定、名称を「田主丸古墳群」に変更{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|2656|田主丸古墳群}}。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[福岡県]][[久留米市]]田主丸町石垣（大塚古墳歴史公園内） '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道：[[九州旅客鉄道]]（JR九州）[[久大本線]] [[田主丸駅]]（徒歩約40分） '''周辺''' * 田主丸古墳群 ** 寺徳古墳 ** 中原狐塚古墳 ** 西館古墳 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 史跡説明板（久留米市2015年設置板ほか） * 地方自治体発行 ** {{Cite {{Infobox Kofun | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurume, Fukuoka|qq=}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurume, Fukuoka|qq=}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurume, Fukuoka|qq=}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurume, Fukuoka|qq=}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Kurume, Fukuoka|ja|久留米市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurume, Fukuoka|qq=}}, Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
== References == {{Reflist}}
== External Links == * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656 '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site''' (Agency for Cultural Affairs, Japan)]

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

== External Links == * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656 '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site''' (Agency for Cultural Affairs, Japan)]

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 33.3262 | coordinates = 130.7115 | region = Japan | type = [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''
