'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]][[Category: of Ōtsuka Kofun History Park|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
== Historic Site == '''National Historic Site''' * '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (as part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''') ** '''Designated in 2002 (Heisei 14)'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/>
== location & Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.

== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|33.326158|N|130.711542|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") | architectural_styles= {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | part_of= {{ill|Tanushimaru Kofun Cluster|WD=Q124818740}} }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (田主丸大塚古墳) is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun) located in [[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan. It is part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This large keyhole-shaped tumulus was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the Chikugo Plain, at the northern foothills of the Mino Mountains (耳納山地).<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The Tanushimaru Kofun Group includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the Teratoku Kofun, Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun, and Nishidate Kofun, but Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The front section of the mound has been significantly leveled due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was mentioned as early as the Edo period in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple archaeological excavations have since been conducted.
The tumulus is keyhole-shaped with the front section facing southward on a slope.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving), arranged in a stone embankment style.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A [[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi) is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a [[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室), but its interior remains unexplored.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the late 6th century,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased after the [[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its large map_size, the kofun's construction background is considered significant.
Additionally, Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications, such as the nearby [[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In 1993, the kofun was Historic Site1 as a municipal historic site,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in 2002, it was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園) and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * Edo period: Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * 1977: Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * 1992: Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * 1993: Designated as a municipal historic site.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * 1995-2001: 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is keyhole-shaped, not circular.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * 2002: National Historic Site Historic Site (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * 2005: Northern section conservation work. * 2006, 2013: 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * 2013-2014: Second phase of conservation work.<ref><nowiki>{{Cite web|url=</nowiki>https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html%7Ctitle=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Kurume|Kurume, Fukuoka]], Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)

== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''[[:en:Iwai Rebellion|Iwai Rebellion]] (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''[[:en:Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|Korasan Kōgoishi]] (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=keyhole-shaped tumulus}} (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''{{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''{{ill|Iwai Rebellion|en|Iwai Rebellion|WD=Q3138004|lt=Iwai Rebellion}} (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''{{ill|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|en|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|WD=Q46999756|lt=Korasan Kōgoishi}} (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|33.326158|N|130.711542|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") | architectural_styles= {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | part_of= {{ill|Tanushimaru Kofun Cluster|WD=Q124818740}} }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=keyhole-shaped tumulus}} (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''{{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''{{ill|Iwai Rebellion|en|Iwai Rebellion|WD=Q3138004|lt=Iwai Rebellion}} (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''{{ill|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|en|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|WD=Q46999756|lt=Korasan Kōgoishi}} (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|33.326158|N|130.711542|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") | architectural_styles= {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | part_of= {{ill|Tanushimaru Kofun Cluster|WD=Q124818740}} }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=keyhole-shaped tumulus}} (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''{{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''{{ill|Iwai Rebellion|en|Iwai Rebellion|WD=Q3138004|lt=Iwai Rebellion}} (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''{{ill|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|en|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|WD=Q46999756|lt=Korasan Kōgoishi}} (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=keyhole-shaped tumulus|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka|1=Kurume}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''{{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''{{ill|Iwai Rebellion|en|Iwai Rebellion|WD=Q3138004|lt=Iwai Rebellion|1=Iwai Rebellion}} (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''{{ill|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|en|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|WD=Q46999756|lt=Korasan Kōgoishi|1=Kōra-san Kōgoishi}} (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun | native_name = 田主丸大塚古墳 | image = {{image requested|cat=Kurume, Fukuoka}} | location = {{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka|1=Kurume}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|33.326158|N|130.711542|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 103m | burial = {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (horizontal stone chamber) | built = Late 6th century (Kofun period) | person = Unknown | burial goods = | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (part of the "Tanushimaru Kofun Group") | architectural_styles= {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpōkōenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | part_of= {{ill|Tanushimaru Kofun Cluster|WD=Q124818740|1=Tanushimaru Kofun Cluster}} }}
'''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun''' (田主丸大塚古墳) is a '''{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=keyhole-shaped tumulus|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} (前方後円墳, zenpō-kōen-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|WD=Q320934|lt=Kurume, Fukuoka|1=Kurume}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' and has been Historic Site1 as a '''National Historic Site''' (史跡) of Japan.<ref name="National Historic Site">{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2656|title=Tanushimaru Kofun Group - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>
== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''{{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''{{ill|Iwai Rebellion|en|Iwai Rebellion|WD=Q3138004|lt=Iwai Rebellion|1=Iwai Rebellion}} (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''{{ill|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|en|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|WD=Q46999756|lt=Korasan Kōgoishi|1=Kōra-san Kōgoishi}} (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)
'''Nearby Sites''' * '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' ** '''Teratoku Kofun''' ** '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''' ** '''Nishidate Kofun'''

== Overview == This '''large keyhole-shaped tumulus''' was constructed on a plateau (elevation: 70-80m) overlooking the '''Chikugo Plain''', at the northern foothills of the '''Mino Mountains (耳納山地)'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> The '''Tanushimaru Kofun Group''' includes several [[decorated kofun]], such as the '''Teratoku Kofun''', '''Nakabaru Kitsunezuka Kofun''', and '''Nishidate Kofun''', but '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun is the largest in the group'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2004}}</ref>
The '''front section of the mound has been significantly leveled''' due to historical land cultivation.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> This kofun was '''mentioned as early as the Edo period''' in historical texts such as the *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* (筑後将士軍談).<ref>{{Harvid|Historic Site of the Region|2008|pp=1-4}}</ref> Multiple '''archaeological excavations''' have since been conducted.
The tumulus is '''keyhole-shaped''' with the '''front section facing southward on a slope'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> No '''{{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} clay figures''' have been found,<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> but the mound was '''covered in [[fukiishi]] (葺石, stone paving)''', arranged in a '''stone embankment style'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> A '''[[Platform-style projection|terrace-like projection]] (造出, tsukuridashi)''' is attached to the rear section.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> The burial chamber is a '''[[Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|horizontal stone chamber]] (横穴式石室)''', but its interior remains '''unexplored'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
The kofun was constructed in the '''late 6th century''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> during a time when the '''building of keyhole-shaped tumuli had largely ceased''' after the '''{{ill|Iwai Rebellion|en|Iwai Rebellion|WD=Q3138004|lt=Iwai Rebellion|1=Iwai Rebellion}} (磐井の乱, early 6th century)'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=17-21}}</ref> Given its '''large map_size''', the kofun's '''construction background is considered significant'''.
Additionally, '''Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun may have connections to ancient mountain fortifications''', such as the nearby '''{{ill|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|en|Kōra-san_Kōgoishi|WD=Q46999756|lt=Korasan Kōgoishi|1=Kōra-san Kōgoishi}} (高良山神籠石, Korasan Castle)'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1060manabi/2050bunkazai/3020maibuncenter/2014-0610-1528-551.html|title=4th Kōgoishi Summit Pamphlet|publisher=Kurume City Official Website}}</ref>
In '''1993''', the kofun was Historic Site1 as a '''municipal historic site''',<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> and in '''2002''', it was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''.<ref name="National Historic Site"/> It has since been developed into '''Ōtsuka Kofun History Park (大塚古墳歴史公園)''' and is open to the public.
== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)

== Excavation History == * '''Edo period''': Recorded in *Chikugo Shōshi Gundan* as "The Greatest Ōtsuka of this Province".<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1977''': Listed in the *Fukuoka Prefecture Archaeological map* as a "circular mound" (大塚3号墳).<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''1992''': Preliminary survey by the typeer Tanushimaru Town Board of Education.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''1993''': Designated as a '''municipal historic site'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> * '''1995-2001''': 1st-5th excavations reveal that the mound is '''keyhole-shaped, not circular'''.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun|2001|pp=1-3}}</ref> * '''2002''': '''National Historic Site Historic Site''' (as part of the Tanushimaru Kofun Group).<ref name="National Historic Site"/> * '''2005''': Northern section conservation work. * '''2006, 2013''': 6th-7th excavations.<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun II|2014|pp=1-2}}</ref> * '''2013-2014''': Second phase of conservation work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.kurume.fukuoka.jp/1500soshiki/9125bunkazai/3010oshirase/2015-0323-1253-551.html|title=Completion tier 6]], Tanushimaru Town, Ishigaki (within Ōtsuka Kofun History Park)
'''Access''' * '''Train''': '''JR Kyudai Main Line (久大本線), Tanushimaru Station''' (40-minute walk)

== Mound area == The tumulus is '''103 meters in length''':<ref>{{Harvid|Tanushimaru Ōtsuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}</ref> * '''Rear section''': 60m in diameter * '''Front section''': 45m in width
The '''front section has been heavily damaged''' and is only represented by a '''stylized reconstruction'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/>
A '''terrace-like projection (造出, tsukuridashi)''' extends from the '''western rear section'''.<ref name="Explanatory Sign"/> It measures: * '''Width (rear side)''': 11.5m * '''Width (tip side)''': 7.5m * '''Length''': 12.3m
